PySpark Interview Cheatsheet, I wish I had this while preparing for Data Engineering Interviews. 🔻
1/ Optimizing Joins with Broadcast
What it does: Broadcasts smaller DataFrame to all nodes to avoid shuffle in joins.
How to apply:
from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
df_large.join(broadcast(df_small), "id")
Use Case: Joining a large fact table with a small dimension table efficiently.
2/ Handling Skewed Data in GroupBy
What it does: Mitigates data skew by salting keys to balance partitions.
How to apply:
df.withColumn("salt", (rand() * 10).cast("int")).groupBy("key", "salt").agg(...)
Use Case: Reducing hotspot partitions in aggregations on skewed keys.
3/ Dynamic Partition Overwrite
What it does: Overwrites specific partitions without affecting others.
How to apply:
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.sources.partitionOverwriteMode", "dynamic")
df.write.partitionBy("date").mode("overwrite").parquet("path")
Use Case: Updating specific date partitions in a data lake.
4/ Window Functions with Custom Frames
What it does: Defines precise row ranges for window calculations.
How to apply:
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
w = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("date").rowsBetween(-6, 0)
df.withColumn("rolling_avg", avg("sales").over(w))
Use Case: Calculating 7-day moving averages for sales trends.
5/ Caching vs Persist with Storage Levels
What it does: Persists DataFrame with specific storage levels for performance.
How to apply:
df.persist(pyspark.StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)
Use Case: Optimizing iterative ML pipelines with memory and disk spillover.
6/ Handling Nulls in Complex Joins
What it does: Manages nulls explicitly to avoid incorrect join results.
How to apply:
df1.join(df2, (df1.id == df2.id) & (df1.id.isNotNull()), "left")
Use Case: Ensuring accurate results in joins with incomplete data.
7/ Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)
What it does: Dynamically optimizes query plans at runtime.
How to apply:
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
Use Case: Improving performance in skewed joins or aggregations automatically.
8/ Incremental Processing with Delta Lake
What it does: Enables upsert operations for incremental data updates.
How to apply:
from delta.tables import DeltaTable
DeltaTable.forPath(spark, "path").alias("t").merge(df.alias("s"), "t.id = s.id")...
Use Case: Updating a data warehouse with streaming or batch data.
9/ Repartition vs Coalesce Strategically
What it does: Adjusts DataFrame partitions for optimal processing.
How to apply:
df.repartition(10, "key") or df.coalesce(5)
Use Case: Repartition for parallelism, coalesce to reduce shuffle overhead.
